about: One plain base airframe per physical type flown by New Zealand's scheduled airlines. Approve these first, then repaint each into airline liveries using the approved image as the reference.

types.name: Airbus A320-200
types.check: 2 turbofans · 1 fin · 2 wings · sharklets · 37.6 m long, 35.8 m span
anatomy: Narrow-body twin-jet airliner, low wing, conventional tail (one vertical fin, two horizontal stabilisers set low on the rear fuselage).
EXACTLY 2 engines: one large turbofan slung under each wing, close to the ground, round intake, no engines on the tail.
Wings swept back about 25 degrees with a single upturned sharklet at each wingtip.
Fuselage length is about 1.05 times the wingspan (37.6 m long, 35.8 m span); round tube, pointed cone nose, slightly upswept tail cone.
Two passenger doors each side (one forward, one aft of the wings) and two small overwing exits.

types.name: Airbus A320neo
types.check: 2 larger turbofans with serrated nozzles · 1 fin · 2 wings · 37.6 m long
anatomy: Same airframe layout as an A320-200: narrow-body twin-jet, low swept wing, one vertical fin, two horizontal stabilisers.
EXACTLY 2 engines, one under each wing: visibly LARGER-diameter turbofans than the old A320, mounted slightly further forward of the wing, with a serrated (chevron) edge on the rear nozzle.
Large blended sharklet winglets at each wingtip.
Fuselage length about 1.05 times the wingspan (37.6 m long, 35.8 m span).
Two passenger doors each side plus two small overwing exits.

types.name: Airbus A321neo
types.check: 2 large turbofans · 1 fin · 2 wings · STRETCHED fuselage 44.5 m, 35.8 m span
anatomy: Stretched narrow-body twin-jet: same wing, tail and engines as an A320neo but with a much LONGER fuselage, about 1.24 times the wingspan (44.5 m long, 35.8 m span).
EXACTLY 2 large-diameter turbofans, one under each wing, serrated rear nozzle edge.
Large blended sharklet winglets; one vertical fin, two horizontal stabilisers.
Four passenger doors each side (two ahead of the wing, two behind it) plus overwing exits.

types.name: ATR 72-600
types.airlines: Air New Zealand (Air Chathams flies the near-identical ATR 72-500: reuse this airframe)
types.check: 2 turboprops · 6-blade props · HIGH straight wing · T-tail · 27.2 m long, 27.1 m span
anatomy: Twin-turboprop regional airliner with a HIGH, straight, nearly untapered wing mounted on top of the fuselage.
EXACTLY 2 engines in nacelles on top of the wing, each with a SIX-bladed propeller. Long nacelle bulges extend behind the wing's trailing edge to house the main landing gear.
T-TAIL: one vertical fin with the horizontal stabiliser mounted at the very top of the fin.
Fuselage length about equal to the wingspan (27.2 m long, 27.1 m span); round barrel, short pointed nose with weather-radar radome.
Passenger door aft on the left side, a smaller cargo door behind it is optional; large oval cabin windows.

types.name: De Havilland Canada Dash 8 Q300
types.check: 2 turboprops · 4-blade props · HIGH wing · T-tail · 25.7 m long, 27.4 m span
anatomy: Twin-turboprop regional airliner with a HIGH wing and long slender fuselage with a drooping, rounded nose.
EXACTLY 2 engines in long nacelles on the wing, each with a FOUR-bladed propeller; the nacelles extend well behind the wing's trailing edge (main gear folds into them).
T-TAIL: one tall vertical fin with the horizontal stabiliser at the very top.
Wingspan slightly greater than fuselage length (25.7 m long, 27.4 m span).
Passenger door aft on the left side, small rectangular cabin windows.

types.name: Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner
types.check: 2 turbofans · 1 fin · 2 wings · raked tips, NO winglets · 62.8 m long, 60.1 m span
anatomy: Wide-body twin-jet, low wing, one vertical fin, two horizontal stabilisers.
EXACTLY 2 very large turbofans, one under each wing, with serrated (chevron) rear nacelle edges.
Long, gracefully curved, strongly swept wings with RAKED wingtips (swept-back tips): NO upturned winglets and NO sharklets.
Smooth, rounded nose with a dark cockpit window band; large oval cabin windows (the 787 windows are tall and rounded).
Fuselage length about 1.04 times the wingspan (62.8 m long, 60.1 m span).

types.name: Boeing 777-300ER
types.check: 2 HUGE turbofans · 1 fin · 2 wings · raked tips · 73.9 m long, 64.8 m span · 6-wheel main bogies
anatomy: Very long wide-body twin-jet, low wing, one vertical fin, two horizontal stabilisers.
EXACTLY 2 enormous turbofans, one under each wing, each nearly as wide as a narrow-body's fuselage; round smooth intake, no chevrons required.
Swept wings with RAKED (swept-back) wingtips: NO winglets.
Fuselage length clearly greater than the wingspan (73.9 m long, 64.8 m span), with a long tube, pointed tail cone and round cockpit nose.
Main landing gear with two six-wheel bogies (retracted when airborne; keep the hull clean).

types.name: Saab 340
types.check: 2 turboprops · 3-blade props · LOW wing · conventional tail · 19.7 m long, 21.4 m span
anatomy: Twin-turboprop regional airliner with a LOW straight wing and a short, round, tubular fuselage with a blunt rounded nose.
EXACTLY 2 engines in nacelles on the wing, each with a THREE-bladed propeller.
Conventional tail: one vertical fin with the horizontal stabiliser mounted low on the fuselage.
Wingspan slightly greater than fuselage length (19.7 m long, 21.4 m span).
Passenger door aft on the left, small rounded-rectangle cabin windows.

types.name: Cessna 206 Stationair
types.check: 1 piston engine · 1 propeller · HIGH wing with 1 strut each side · fixed tricycle gear · 8.6 m long, 10.9 m span
anatomy: Single-engine light utility aeroplane with a HIGH, straight, rectangular wing.
EXACTLY ONE engine in the nose with a single THREE-bladed propeller.
ONE straight support strut from the lower fuselage to each wing (two struts in total).
Fixed (non-retracting) tricycle landing gear with a nose wheel and two main wheels, wheel fairings optional.
Conventional tail: one vertical fin, two horizontal stabilisers, with a small dorsal fillet.
Short fat fuselage (8.6 m long, 10.9 m span); large rear double cargo doors are optional.

types.name: British Aerospace Jetstream 31
types.check: 2 turboprops · 4-blade props · LOW wing · conventional tail · 14.4 m long, 15.9 m span
anatomy: Small twin-turboprop commuter with a LOW straight wing and a slim, round fuselage with a long pointed nose.
EXACTLY 2 engines in slim nacelles on the wing, each with a FOUR-bladed propeller.
Conventional tail: one vertical fin, two horizontal stabilisers set low on the rear fuselage.
Small square-ish cabin windows, one airstair passenger door aft on the left.
Wingspan slightly greater than fuselage length (14.4 m long, 15.9 m span).

types.name: British Aerospace Jetstream 32
types.airlines: Originair (exterior near-identical to the JS31: reuse if the JS31 airframe is approved)
types.check: 2 turboprops · 4-blade props · LOW wing · conventional tail · 14.4 m long, 15.9 m span
anatomy: Small twin-turboprop commuter with a LOW straight wing and a slim, round fuselage with a long pointed nose (same exterior as a Jetstream 31).
EXACTLY 2 engines in slim nacelles on the wing, each with a FOUR-bladed propeller.
Conventional tail: one vertical fin, two horizontal stabilisers set low on the rear fuselage.
Small square-ish cabin windows, one airstair passenger door aft on the left.

types.name: Cessna 208B Grand Caravan
types.airlines: Sounds Air, Barrier Air (one airframe serves both)
types.check: 1 turboprop · 1 prop · HIGH wing, 1 strut each side · fixed gear · belly pod · 12.7 m long, 15.9 m span
anatomy: Large single-engine utility turboprop with a HIGH, straight, rectangular wing.
EXACTLY ONE turboprop engine in a long smooth nose with a single THREE-bladed propeller and a ring-shaped exhaust on the left of the nose.
ONE straight support strut from the lower fuselage to each wing (two struts in total).
Fixed tricycle landing gear with fairings on all three wheels; a long cargo pod slung under the belly.
Conventional tail: one vertical fin with a dorsal fillet, two horizontal stabilisers.
Long, tall, boxy cabin with four to five small square windows each side; stretched 208B body (12.7 m long, 15.9 m span).

types.name: Britten-Norman BN-2 Islander
types.check: 2 piston engines · 2 propellers · HIGH wing · fixed gear · boxy fuselage · 10.9 m long, 14.9 m span
anatomy: Small twin-piston-engine utility aeroplane with a HIGH, straight, rectangular wing.
EXACTLY 2 engines, one in a nacelle on each wing, each with its own propeller.
Fixed tricycle landing gear with the main wheels in small pods under each engine nacelle.
Very boxy, slab-sided fuselage with a short rounded nose and large windows along the cabin (10.9 m long, 14.9 m span).
Conventional tail: one tall vertical fin with a swept leading edge, two horizontal stabilisers.

types.name: Cessna 185 Skywagon
types.check: 1 piston engine · 1 propeller · HIGH wing with 1 strut each side · TAILDRAGGER · 7.8 m long, 10.9 m span
anatomy: Single-engine light utility aeroplane with a HIGH, straight, rectangular wing.
EXACTLY ONE engine in the nose with a single propeller.
ONE straight support strut from the lower fuselage to each wing (two struts in total).
TAILWHEEL layout: two main wheels forward and a small tailwheel at the rear (taildragger), the nose sits high with the tail low.
One vertical fin, two horizontal stabilisers, a short fuselage (7.8 m long, 10.9 m span).

types.name: Piper PA-32 Cherokee Six
types.check: 1 piston engine · 1 propeller · LOW wing, no struts · fixed tricycle gear · 8.4 m long, 10.0 m span
anatomy: Single-engine light six-seat touring aeroplane with a LOW, straight, untapered rectangular wing and NO wing struts.
EXACTLY ONE engine in the nose with a single TWO-bladed propeller.
Fixed tricycle landing gear: one nose wheel and two main wheels under the wings.
Conventional tail: one vertical fin and one all-moving horizontal stabiliser (stabilator) low on the rear fuselage.
Long cabin with three windows each side, 8.4 m long, 10.0 m span.

types.name: Boeing 737-300 freighter
types.check: 2 turbofans · 1 fin · 2 wings · NO winglets · flat-bottomed engines · windowless freighter · 33.4 m long, 28.9 m span
anatomy: Narrow-body twin-jet freighter, low wing, one vertical fin, two horizontal stabilisers.
EXACTLY 2 engines, one under each wing: small-diameter turbofans with a flattened, oval underside because they sit very close to the ground.
Wings swept back with plain wingtips: NO winglets, NO sharklets.
Freighter conversion: NO passenger windows along the cabin (a solid fuselage), with only the cockpit windows, and a large cargo door on the left forward fuselage.
Fuselage length clearly longer than the wingspan (33.4 m long, 28.9 m span).

types.name: Boeing 737-400 freighter
types.check: 2 turbofans · 1 fin · 2 wings · NO winglets · flat-bottomed engines · windowless freighter · 36.4 m long, 28.9 m span
anatomy: Stretched 737-300: same layout, narrow-body twin-jet freighter with a slightly longer fuselage (36.4 m long, 28.9 m span).
EXACTLY 2 engines, one under each wing: small-diameter turbofans with a flattened, oval underside.
Wings swept back with plain wingtips: NO winglets, NO sharklets.
Freighter conversion: NO passenger windows along the cabin, a large cargo door on the left forward fuselage.
One vertical fin, two horizontal stabilisers.

not_included: Not covered: the Boeing 787-10 (on order, not yet flying) and any airline whose fleet could not be verified (Parcelair, Texel Air, Sunair, Golden Bay Air, Air Safaris, Glenorchy Air, Air Kaikoura, Air Napier, Salt Air). The blade counts on the Saab 340, Jetstream, Islander and C185 are the ones I am least sure of: if your reference photos show something different, say so and I will correct the spec.
